REQUIREMENTS FOR PACKING OF PESTICIDES
PART ( 1 SOLID PESTICIDES

Second Revision )
0. FOREWORD
( Second of Indian the draft Sectional Marine, Division Since the packing requirements covered in this standard have been adopted by the Registration Committee constituted under the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 1968, this standard assumes statutory character. 0.3 The list of Indian Standards relating to packaging referred to in this standard is given in Appendix A. 0.4 This standard has been published in four parts: this part ( Part 1 ) covers the requirements for packing of solid pesticides. The other parts are: Part Part Part 2 3 4 Liquid pesticides pesticides

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau Standards on 3 October 1<988, after finalized by the Packaging of Chemicals Committee had been approved by the Cargo Movement and Packaging Council.

0.2 This standard, issued in 1976, was first revised in 1980. This second revision has been undertaken to incorporate the packing requirements for pesticides as modified through various amendments issued subsequently and also to include packing requirements for some pesticides for which the related Indian Standard Specifications have been published in the meanwhile. For some pesticides, techxiical and their formulations, the packing requirements have been suitably wherever new/alternative packing changed materials have been approved. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ments for packing ( Part 1 ) covers the of solid pesticides. require-

Household Fumigants

1.2 This standard does not cover the packing requirements for solid pesticides meant for household use and fumigants. 2. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

2.3 The high density polyethylene ( HDPE ) used in the fabrication of HDPE container or its components shall be of designation HDPE 43BA, 42BA or 42BB having melt flow index ( i6 ) not more than 1.8 g/l0 minutes ( see IS : 7328-1974 j. 2.4 Containers made of mild steel and tinplate shall be painted/lacquered externally to prevent rusting if not lithographed. If lithographed, top and bottom components shall be lacquered externa!ly. 2.5 Heat-sealing of the containers and machine stitching of the bags ( see 2.7 ) shall be such that no material comes out from the seams/seals during normal handling. 2.6 Closures, wherever provided, shall be leakproof and temper-proof. The stitching thread of the bags shall be sealed with the metal seal at both ends or the temperproofness shall be secured by any other suitable means. 2.7 Double hessian jute bags ( see IS : 8115-1976 ), DW tarpaulin laminated jute bags ( see IS : 81171976), HDPE woven sacks [ see IS: 8069 (Part l)1981 ] and HDPE woven bags [see IS : 8069 ( Part 2).1981 1, used for packing pesticides, 1

2.1 The solid pesticides, technical and their formulations, shal1 be packed in containers in the quantities of 100 g, 250 g, 500 g, 1 kg, 5 kg, 10 kg, 20 kg, 25 kg and 50 kg each. Further technical grade pesticides meant for bulk consumption may also be packed in containers in the quantities of 100 kg and 200 kg each. `Formulated granules can also be packed in containers in the quantity of 2 kg each. Any other quantity per pack specified in Tables 1 to 4 is in addition to the quantity per pack specified above. 2.2 Retail packs up to 1 kg shall be further packed in corrugated fibreboard boxes [see IS : 2771 ( Part 1 )-1977 ] or wooden cases ( see IS : 1503-1979 ) when they require transportation.

IS : 8190 ( Part 1) - 1988 wherever allowed, shall be provided with an internal loose LDPE liner of thickness not less than 0.062 mm and in the form of tubular sheath, bottom sealed. Alternatively, loose liner may also be of HM-HDPE of thickness not less than 0 031 mm, wherever expressively specified so in Tables 1 to 4. The length and breadth of the loose liner shall be 10 and 5 percent more, respectively,<ahan those of the outer bag. 2.8 For the individual pack of 5 kg and above in case of encapsulated granules ( see Table 4 ), hand-gloves shall also be provided. 2.9 The containers shall be of sturdy design and shall conform to the relevant Indian Standards, as given in the text. 3. SPECIFIC REQUYREMENTS 3.1 Technical Grade Pesticides

nical grade pesticides shall be packed in dry and clean containers as described in Table 1. 3.2 Dusting Powders - The dusting powders shall be packed in dry and clean containers as described in Table 2. 3.3 Water Dispersible Powder Concentrates - The eater dispersible powder concentrates shall be packed in clean and dry containers as described in Table 3. 3.4 Granules - The granules in clean and dry containers Table 4. shall be packed as described in

3.5 Other Solid Formulations - Solid pesticides other than technical, dusting powders, water dispersible powder concentrates and granules shall be packed in dry and clean containers as described in Table 5.
